source.title: Towards mechanistic understanding in a data-driven weather model: internal activations reveal interpretable physical features

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or truncation; the complete paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Extends sparse-autoencoder feature analysis to GraphCast, a data-driven weather model, and reports feature-probing and intervention results. It does not test toy-model superposition geometry or LLM representations.
record.gate_note: The study applies SAEs to GraphCast and reports probes comparing SAE features with single-neuron activations, plus interventions on one SAE feature. It does not measure overlap, near-orthogonality, interference, capacity competition, or a sparsity-dependent geometric transition. The figures report additional results that are not numerically stated in the text; figure-only values are recorded as such.
record.test_reason: The study applies k-sparse SAEs to a trained real network, the GraphCast weather GNN, and compares single-feature probes against single-neuron probes. That is indirect evidence of dictionary-recoverable features spread across neurons (V4), but in a non-LLM system. It does not test toy geometry, capacity competition, canonical units or feature dimensionality. The interventions measure steering of storm predictions, not superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors say SAEs extract highly interpretable physical features from GraphCast, and that modifying a TC feature yields correct, physics-constrained changes. They caveat that this is shown for a single model, that the sea-ice features are correlational only, and that completeness and self-repair are open questions.
record.recipe_differences: Applies k-sparse autoencoders and feature probes/interventions to a trained weather GNN; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: SAE latent dimension and sparsity are varied. The authors report that intermediate latent dimensions (nl=2048, 4096) seem optimal for tropical-cyclone prediction and hypothesize that feature splitting at larger dictionaries may affect probe performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Scaling SAE feature 3243 by 1+γ at each step monotonically strengthens or weakens predicted Hurricane Ida; γ=0.5 gives a runaway, unphysical response.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intervening on an SAE feature in a weather model causally steers a physical prediction, with physical consistency kept for moderate modifications.

record.problems: The study analyzes one weather model. Several reported outcomes are presented in figures without numerical values in the text. It describes the sea-ice feature result as correlation rather than causal evidence, and notes that feature completeness and possible self-repair remain unresolved.
record.rows_left_out: Left out other seasonal and diurnal feature maps, the atmospheric-river neuron comparison map, and the mass-continuity, hydrostatic-balance, and gradient-wind diagnostic curves. These are in Figures 2, 5D-F, and 8; they do not directly measure the claim versions about superposition geometry, capacity competition, or canonical feature units.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, overlap, near-orthogonality, interference or sparsity-dependent transition.
All: no measurement of importance versus dedicated or shared dimensions.
All: polysemanticity is mentioned only as background.
LLMs specifically; the study covers a weather GNN only. No direct measure of how many neurons each feature spans.
Completeness, stability and canonicity. Feature splitting at larger nl is hypothesized only. Self-repair and completeness are left to future work.

missing.what: No SAE feature found for atmospheric blocking events across all hyperparameters (best F1 0.1).
SAEs trained on randomly initialized GraphCast also yield diurnal and seasonal features, but mainly region-specific ones. This is a control on what the SAE recovers from data versus the model.
TC probe F1 across k and nl, with intermediate nl (2048, 4096) best; feature splitting is hypothesized for larger dictionaries.

record.verdict_notes: V4 names LLMs, and GraphCast is a weather GNN. The V4 labels are therefore an extension to a new kind of system (T3), and a researcher may prefer to treat them as out of scope. The study is not an original source. No uncertainty is reported on the F1 scores.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model feature overlap, near-orthogonality, interference, and sparsity-dependent transition.
Whether feature importance determines dedicated dimensions versus shared capacity.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure, and whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.
The study tests SAE feature recovery in GraphCast, not LLMs; it does not measure features distributed across many neurons. Its results extend indirect SAE evidence to a weather model.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features. The study notes possible feature splitting but does not establish feature stability or completeness.
Whether underlying superposed features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relationships.condition: GraphCast (36.7M weather GNN, not an LLM), layer 8, k=32 nl=4096 SAE, tropical-cyclone probing
relationships.reason: A single SAE feature predicts TC presence (F1 0.48) while the best single neuron is near random (0.01), so the feature is dictionary-recoverable but not neuron-aligned (r1, r2).
relationships.display_finding: A single SAE feature predicted tropical-cyclone presence with F1 0.48, while the best single neuron was near random at 0.01, so the feature is recoverable by the dictionary but not aligned with neurons.

relationships.condition: GraphCast: atmospheric-river and blocking-event probes, and dependence on SAE size
relationships.reason: The AR neuron probe reaches F1 0.30, so the SAE advantage is small (r4, r3). Per the text, no blocking-event feature was found (best F1 0.1), and TC recovery peaks at intermediate nl.
relationships.display_finding: A neuron probe for atmospheric rivers reached F1 0.30, leaving the SAE only a small advantage. No blocking-event feature was found (best F1 0.1), and tropical-cyclone recovery peaked at an intermediate SAE size.
